question: Suppose $L$ is a language which contains the empty word, the word $\alpha$ and the word $\beta$, and has the property that whenever $P$ and $Q$ are in $L$, the word $P\cdot Q$ is also in $L$. The smallest such $L$ is

options.A: the language consisting of all possible words
options.C: the language containing precisely the words of the form $\alpha^{n_1}\beta^{n_1}\alpha^{n_2}\beta^{n_2}\cdots\alpha^{n_k}\beta^{n_k}$, where $k$ is any positive integer and $n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_k$ are nonnegative integers

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
